# Agent Joules build log

Purpose: the single record of toolchain facts, version deviations, scan results, test counts, per-ID filter results, probe and WSL2 notes, user actions, requirements that cannot be met and base commits (REQ-002, REQ-029, builder standing order 6). ASCII only, LF only; never a key value, a hostname or an IP. Every number carries one label: measured, user-reported, inferred or assumed.

## Toolchain check

Commands, exit codes, UTC dates and labels of the SDK, Docker, WSL2, Ollama, GPU driver and git checks (AJ-002), plus the hygiene, property and grep checks that later M0 stories run.

### AJ-001 checks (2026-10-18T16:17:53Z, measured)

| Check | Command | Exit code | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| nine headings once each | for each of the nine headings: `grep -cxF "<heading>" docs/build-log.md`; a count other than 1 prints `missing heading: <heading>` and the loop exits 1 | 0 | every count is 1 |
| ASCII only | `grep -nP "[^\x00-\x7F]" docs/build-log.md` | 1 | no match |
| LF only, story command | `grep -c $'\r' docs/build-log.md` | prints 0 | printed 0; the M0 peer reviewer measured that GNU grep 3.0 does count CR bytes when bash expands `$'\r'`, so a 0 on a CRLF file came from the executor's POSIX-sh shell not expanding `$'\r'`, not from grep; the byte count on the next row is the binding check |
| LF only, byte count | `tr -cd '\r' < docs/build-log.md` followed by `wc -c` | prints 0 | 0 CR bytes |
| no key pattern | `grep -nE "nvapi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}" docs/build-log.md` | 1 | no match |
| negative, scratch copy: deleted heading | the heading loop on a copy without `## Test counts` | 1 | printed `missing heading: ## Test counts` |
| negative, scratch copy: non-ASCII dash | `grep -nP "[^\x00-\x7F]"` on a copy with an em-dash appended | 0 | reported the offending line number (44) |
| scratch copy: a row appended under an existing heading | one row appended under `## Secret scan`, then `grep -cxF "## Secret scan"` | prints 1 | heading count unchanged, no new heading |

Working-tree line endings (2026-10-18T16:22Z, measured with `tr -cd '\r' < <file>` and `wc -c`): `.editorconfig` has 389 CR bytes in 389 lines and `.gitignore` 482 CR bytes in 499 lines, so both are CRLF in the working tree (`git ls-files --eol` prints `i/lf w/crlf`; `core.autocrlf=true`). README.md, .gitattributes and the docs/ files are LF. The index is LF for every file. Design section 2.3 states the worktree was LF on 2026-10-18; that is not true for these two files. AJ-009 adds `* text=auto eol=lf` and re-checks the two files out as LF.

## Version deviations and additions

Every package whose used version differs from the pins of design section 2.4 (package, pinned version, used version, reason) and every package added beyond the design list (REQ-002).

Decision (2026-10-18, AJ-005): stay on the prompt pins. The coordinator versions Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.11.0, Microsoft.Agents.AI 1.25.0 and OpenTelemetry 1.20.0 are rejected (design C-01, ADR-20 row 1, open point O-01). `dotnet restore` exit 0 on all 22 pins (measured 16:28Z and 16:36Z); no NuGet audit warning; no deviation recorded. M0 adds no package beyond design section 2.4; M1 story AJ-033 adds the Options packages and records them here as additions.

| Package | Pinned version | Used version | Reason |

Scan of record for AJ-011: `git grep fallback` (gitleaks not installed), exit code 1 (no match), verdict clean, measured first at commit 8635b32 (2026-10-18T16:48:49Z) and re-run at commit 71a1cf4 (2026-10-18T17:07:24Z) after the AJ-008, AJ-009 and AJ-010 commits that touched docs/ and tests/. Rule (broadened on the security reviewer's finding): the scan is re-run on the working tree before each commit until M7 (tracked, untracked and history greps, so the content about to be committed is covered), not only before commits that touch docs/ or config/, because test fixtures under tests/ and src/ are the likelier leak; the latest exit code is the one that counts; each re-run is appended as the next row of the table above, the M0 exit re-run included; future pattern re-runs use `-l` instead of `-n` so a hit prints only the file name. Known limits of the fallback against gitleaks: it cannot catch keys that are not in the current environment, credentials without the `nvapi-` prefix and without a registered value, encoded or split values, dangling objects, or high-entropy strings of unknown shape. Amended 2026-10-18 (post-exit review): the exact-value greps pass the value on stdin, `printf '%s\n' "${!NAME}" | git grep -qF -f -` (also with `--untracked` and over `$(git rev-list --all)`), never as a command-line argument, because an argument is visible in process listings and git traces while git runs; an empty value makes git grep exit 128, so the empty-variable guard stays.

Linux `libnvidia-ml.so.1` then `libnvidia-ml.so`; other platforms empty); `Interop/NvmlLibraryResolver.cs` (`EnsureRegistered()` behind a static `Lazy<bool>` calling `NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver` once for the logical name `nvml`; `LoadPaths` maps the bare Windows candidate to its full path under `Environment.SystemDirectory` and every candidate is loaded with `NativeLibrary.TryLoad(string path, out nint handle)`, the Linux soname by name (direct dlopen); when no candidate loads for `nvml` the resolver throws `DllNotFoundException` naming the candidates, so the runtime's default search never probes the application folder; it returns zero for any other library name; the first non-zero handle is cached with `Interlocked.CompareExchange`; the public `TryLoadFirst(candidates, loader, out handle)` injected-loader overload carries the production sequence); `ToLoadPath(candidate, systemDirectory)` internal and pure (a bare name becomes `<systemDirectory>\nvml.dll` by string concatenation so the Windows list is identical on a Linux runner; a qualified candidate is unchanged); `NvmlApi.cs` (`public sealed class NvmlApi : INvmlApi`; the constructor calls EnsureRegistered; every native code is cast to NvmlReturn, unknown codes pass through as unnamed values; - Security mitigation note (final wording from the security gate, 2026-10-19; also placed in design 5.6):

  Linux and WSL2 (inferred for the cloudgpu VM; measured in Docker on the laptop): the resolver passes `libnvidia-ml.so.1`, then `libnvidia-ml.so`, to `NativeLibrary.TryLoad(name, out h)`, which hands the soname to `dlopen` unchanged. The dynamic loader then searches `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, the executable's `DT_RUNPATH`, `/etc/ld.so.cache` (on WSL2 this includes `/usr/lib/wsl/lib` through `/etc/ld.so.conf.d`), then `/lib` and `/usr/lib`. The .NET host's native-library folders, including the application folder of a self-contained publish, are not probed. When neither soname loads, the resolver throws `DllNotFoundException`, so the runtime's default search never runs. Anyone who can set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` can already inject code through `LD_PRELOAD` or `DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS`, so no privilege boundary is crossed. Operating rules: run the CLI as an unprivileged user, never as root; never run it with an `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` that contains an empty entry or `.`, because `dlopen` reads those as the current directory; keep `artifacts/linux-x64` on the VM writable only by the deploying user.

  Windows (measured 2026-10-19): `nvml.dll` is loaded by its full path under `Environment.SystemDirectory`. Its static imports are `KERNEL32.dll` and `ADVAPI32.dll` only, both KnownDLLs, so its dependencies never come from the current directory or PATH. The NVSMI fallback is tried only when `ProgramW6432` is a fully qualified path and the System32 copy fails to load. Anyone who controls the environment can already run code in the process.
- Carried forward: AJ-022 builds the `Unavailable` reason from fixed text naming `nvml.dll` or `libnvidia-ml.so.1`, never from the exception message, because the resolver's message lists the full load paths including whatever `ProgramW6432` held (security advisory); the story that adds kernel32 imports to this assembly (`PowerSourceDetector`, design 3.1) must route them to System32 full paths too, since `Resolve` returns zero for other names and the runtime default search probes the host folders first (security advisory); the deprecated-export reader path is proven at the reader level only, the laptop driver has the new export (code-review and spec remark); `Resolve`'s throw path, the NVSMI branch and the Linux branch have not run on the laptop host itself, the Linux branch is measured in Docker (above). A short registered key value (five characters or more) that occurs in a run file or a rendered output refuses the report with nothing written, fail-closed by design; real keys are long random strings (AJ-086 gates, owner: the user at the M3 exit, only if a placeholder key is ever registered).

### AJ-056 Orchestrate a tier run over tasks, repeats and modes (REQ-017, REQ-013, EDGE-005)

- Shipped (builder 12:28Z to 13:07Z, tests written first; battery 1 13:09:23Z to 13:11:27Z): replaced the `RunOrchestrator` placeholder with the production orchestrator. Per selected tier it builds the `MeteringServices` (`SampledEnergyMeter` over the GPU opened again at `Gpu:Index` for `local` and `cloudgpu`, `UnmeteredEnergyMeter` for `nvidia` and `nebius`; the `IMeterGate` chosen by `--mode`; one in-memory sink per tier run, forwarded to `IRunListener`), with `ICostCalculator`, `AgentJoulesInstruments` and the host `TimeProvider`. A measured tier runs the start sequence (GPU port, meter start, warm-up once per distinct model ID, idle baseline for `--baseline-seconds` with `Baseline:MaxCoefficientOfVariation`, the EDGE-005 warning through `ConsoleReporter.ReportBaseline` on stderr). Then every task in file order and every repeat 1..n runs with fresh agents (`AgentFactory.CreateAll`) and a fresh workflow (`AgentJoulesWorkflowFactory.RunAsync`), one `running` checkpoint after each (task, repeat) and a final `completed` write; the meter and the GPU source are disposed in a `finally`. Shutdown (Ctrl+C, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, `ApplicationStopping`): each `cancelled` reading of the interrupted (task, repeat) is copied as `incomplete`, `run.status` becomes `incomplete`, the checkpoint is written with a fresh 10 s wall-clock token, then the cancellation is rethrown and the command exits 5. A shutdown before the first step still writes an incomplete file holding the probe. A `StepFailedException` propagates (exit 5). `RunAssembler` builds the `RunDocument` (run id, tasks, mode, repeat, `startUtc`, tool version and commit, environment, models, totals with labels, checkpoints that carry the totals so far). `ConsoleRunListener` (the Cli implementation of `IRunListener`) prints one line per finished step and the `results:` and `totals:` lines per tier through `ConsoleReporter`. `ReportSentences.ConcurrentOverlap` holds the fixed concurrent-overlap sentence. Seams: `IJudgeService` with `NoOpJudgeService`, `ILocalRuntime` with `LocalRuntimeInfo` and `NoOpLocalRuntime`. The run command's service hook registers the meter gate, the agent factory and `AgentJoulesInstruments` beside the telemetry; `RunPlan` gained `StartUtc` and `OutputDisplay`; `RunCommand` takes the start instant once for every tier's file name. Tests: the feature file `tests/AgentJoules.Specs/Features/Cli/AJ-056-run-orchestration.feature` (identical to the story block), its steps and context; `RunOrchestrationTests` with the nested classes `UnstableBaseline`, `Modes`, `Assembler`, `ConsoleLines` and `Seams`; `FakeTimeDriver` gained a step-cap parameter; `HoldingHttpMessageHandler` holds the n-th completion request for the shutdown scenario; the exit-5 row of `ExitCodeTests.RunCommandCodes` runs the production orchestrator; `FakeRunOrchestrator` stays the double of the AJ-052 to AJ-055 scenarios. Paths changed or new: 24. Fix round (2026-10-21, AJ-056): new files `RunListenerSink` (Workflow/Runs; keeps each reading first, catches every listener failure, holds the `_listenerLock` that serializes the listener calls), `RunLog` (a LoggerMessage class; Debug, exception type only), `TierKinds` (Core/Runs; IsMeasured, IsHosted, used by the orchestrator, the assembler, `PreflightService` and `StepReading`), `MetricLabelText` (Core/Labels; the labels `N/A` and `not-reported` for the JSON converter and the console lines, serialized strings unchanged) and `tests/AgentJoules.UnitTests/RunOrchestrationTests.Shutdown.cs`. `ResultsFileWriter.ThrowIfFileExists` is public and shared with the writer's first write. `HoldingHttpMessageHandler` bounds its hold at 60 s, and the shutdown tests cancel in a `finally`. Shutdown order: the incomplete checkpoint is written before the incomplete step lines are printed; its budget is min(10 s, 12 s minus the time since the signal, on the wall clock) and never below 1 s; a failed write (any exception except the cancellation) is logged at Debug and reported as one stderr warning line, and the command still exits 5; a tier that never started gets no file; a shutdown inside the local baseline wait writes a file with a null baseline, zero steps and every sum not-reported `no-steps`. Cost rule and early file refusal as in the design 3.4 amendment. Tests added: the measured-tier shutdown, the failed shutdown write, the between-tier cancellation, the listener-failure isolation and the published cancelled line; three judge-seam tests (splice back in place, skipped when the judge key is missing, wrong count throws `InvalidOperationException`); GPU release after a failed local step; a production-orchestrator leak proof (the fake key and the task prompt, echoed by the fake models list and the streamed answer, reach neither stdout, stderr nor any file under `results/`); the cost rows (mixed and all-priced) and the console `cost=N/A` row; the existing-file refusal on the fake clock; the REQ-013 trait on the serialized-totals test.

- Decisions: P-1: the interface is `IJudgeService.ScoreAsync(JudgeRequest, ct)` returning `JudgeResult`, with `Steps` every workflow step of the tier run, `Tasks` the plan's tasks and `Services` the tier run's `MeteringServices` with the judge sink. P-2: the orchestrator creates one bare judge sink per tier run, passes the tier's services as a parameter to a stateless singleton, and passes the judge snapshot on every write of the tier. P-3: a hosted `Judge:Tier` (nvidia, nebius) gets a new `UnmeteredEnergyMeter` per call so its readings carry energy N/A `hosted-tier`; a measured `Judge:Tier` equal to the run tier uses the run's meter; any other measured judge tier gives `judge-failed: judge-tier-not-metered` with no call. P-4: one pipeline per judgeable step, built like `AgentFactory` (provider client of `Judge:Tier`, `RateLimitRetryChatClient`, `MeteredChatClient` outermost with one shared `RetryLedger`), identity `Judge` with `JudgedAgent`, one buffered call at Temperature 0, disposed after the call. P-5: `StepIdentity` and `StepReading` gain the optional `JudgedAgent`, written only when non-null, so a judge reading names the agent whose output it scored and no `JudgeReading` type exists. P-6: `totals.judge` keeps tokens and `costByCurrency` only; a hosted judge's N/A `hosted-tier` shows on each judge reading, never as 0 and never summed. P-7: `JudgeService` writes the reason table on its returned copy through `RunAssembler.WithQuality` with `qualityReason` `not-scored` on every unscored row and leaves the derived metrics to `Assemble`. P-8: `JudgeService` owns the four-case rule (`step-not-ok` and `empty-output` without a call, the judge call for the rest), and the orchestrator passes every step and writes no quality. P-9: `selfJudged` is the ordinal equality of `Judge:ModelId` with any request step's ModelId, passed to `BuildRunInfo` for the completed write only and null otherwise. P-10: `AddAgentJoulesJudge(contentRoot)`, modelled on `AddAgentJoulesCost`, registers the service, loads the rubric once at first resolution, and `RunCommand` resolves it so a missing rubric exits 2 before any check, dry run included; a blank `Judge:ModelId` gives `judge-model-not-configured` per step, not an exit code. P-11: the harness keeps the no-op judge unless `UseProductionJudge` is set, registering it before the test's own `extra` so that a test's judge wins. - Decisions: P-1, the selector API as pinned (`RunHeader`, `RunHeaderReader.Read`, `RunFileSelector.Select`, `Latest`, `LatestBaseline`, the records), with full paths as values and lists ordered ordinally by file name; P-2, an unreadable header is a Problem with one reason token and never a skip, so `report` exits 2; P-3, one accept rule for `Latest` and `LatestBaseline` (`completed` or `partial`, no `non-publishable` flag) and a header tier that differs from the file name is the Problem `tier-mismatch`, checked before the status rule; P-4, a baseline row is keyed (Tier, Variant, Task, Agent) and printed after the tier's primary rows with the tier cell `<tier> baseline`, while the selector labels nothing and draws no number (AJ-082 to AJ-084); P-25, the command resolves each `--in` against `CommandHost.WorkingDirectory`, checks its existence and name, and only then calls `Select` (AJ-086); P-a, candidates are names satisfying `RunFileName.IsValid` for the requested tier, and probe, calibration, `.partial` and other names are filtered by name and never opened; P-b, the header is read through `Utf8JsonReader` only, with no call to `RunFileValidator` or `SchemaValidator`; P-c, the unit and Specs tests build their files in a TempWorkspace and read the committed fixtures in place, never writing them; P-d, the selector aggregates nothing across tiers; builder, the file split into `RunHeaderReader.cs` and `RunFileSelector.cs` (the brief allowed the split).
- Deviations: D1, `Select` stops at the first accepted file per (tier, variant), newest first, so `Skipped` and `Problems` list only files newer than the winner, and every file when none is accepted (a corrupt file older than the winner is not reported; test `Files_older_than_the_selected_one_are_not_opened`); the reason is that the report never needs an older file, the story's criterion 2 does not say what the lists must hold, and the design and story record it. D2, `Select` throws `ArgumentException` for a blank input and for an input that is neither a folder nor a name satisfying `RunFileName.IsValid` (the name echoed through `TextEcho`), and `ArgumentNullException` for a null list, while a valid-named missing file and an unlistable folder are the Problem `unreadable`; the reason is that P-25 has the command check names and existence first, so these are contract guards, and `Select` resolves relative paths against the process directory, so AJ-086 passes absolute paths. D3, `Latest` and `LatestBaseline` read only the requested tier, an invalid tier gives `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` through `TierOptions.NameOf`, a missing folder gives `DirectoryNotFoundException`, and the first Problem of that tier throws `InvalidDataException("<file>: <reason>")` (the draft P-1 wording). D4, header reader details beyond P-2: a `run` that is null or not an object is `run-missing`; a `tier` or `status` that is not a string is `tier-unknown` or `status-unknown`; the last of duplicate `tier`, `status` or `flags` members inside `run`, and the first of duplicate top-level `run` members; a JSON error or invalid UTF-8 is `header-not-json`; at exactly 64 KiB one more byte is probed to tell `header-too-long` from `header-not-json`; the reason is that the reviewers verify the bound before any larger read. D5, the values of `Latest` and `LatestBaseline` are full paths; `Skipped` and `Problems` carry the file name only, ordered ordinally by file name, then by reason. D6, the tier-mismatch check runs before the status rule, so a failed file of the wrong tier is a Problem, not a Skip, and a failed or incomplete status wins over `non-publishable` as the skip reason. D7, the Specs steps run the real selector on files built from the committed fixture text with status and flags edited in a TempWorkspace, the unit tests use minimal header texts, and one unit test points `Select` at the committed fixtures folder in place. D8 (two scratchpad files created and deleted, none in the repository) is a note, not a deviation. D9 (fix round), a FIFO named like a run file is `header-not-json` rather than `unreadable` on Unix, because .NET exposes no file type and a FIFO, a character device and an empty file all report size 0, so the size-0 rule refuses all three before any open; the reason is that a read of a FIFO would block. - Shipped on branch milestone/M0-review2: `SecretRedactor.TrimEnds` returns a slice of the original string, decoding runes from both ends and keeping any invalid sequence (a lone surrogate) as visible, so the ends-trimmed form masks a raw echo of a malformed configured value; `RemoveInvisibleCharacters` drops invalid sequences for the clean form; `Register` registers the whole value and each of its CR- or LF-separated lines in up to three forms each (ends-trimmed, clean, rune-normalised with U+FFFD for an echo that passed through UTF-8), after the security gate showed that rejecting a multi-line value whole left a key on one of its lines unmasked and the code-review gate showed that per-line registration alone dropped short lines and newline-stripped echoes; the `RedactingTextWriter` summary is reflowed to 120 columns and states that a leaveOpen writer stays usable after Dispose and drains on every later Dispose (the AJ-034 console wrappers may receive output after the first drain and before the ProcessExit drain) while an owning writer throws; the generic Reqnroll step "the result is ..." asserts exact equality only; `tests/AgentJoules.Specs/Features/Configuration/.gitkeep` deleted because the folder holds a feature file; fifteen tests added over three gate rounds, two of them theories over the seven line terminators (61 cases on Spec=REQ-029). (2) Measured: `TimerTrackingTimeProvider` reported the sampling loop's `PeriodicTimer` (due 0.1 s) to `FakeTimeDriver` as a wait, so under load the driver could advance a 0.1 s step inside a call; a forced interleaving reproduced Planner [2.000, 3.100] and the 3.1 s union; periodic timers are now recorded in `History` but never advanced for, with the regression test `FakeTimeDriverTests.RunWaitsToCompletionAsync_PeriodicTimer_IsRecordedButNeverAdvancedFor` (fails on the old provider); the overlap test keeps its 3 s, 90 J and flag assertions and also asserts that every window is exactly 1 s. (3) Measured on this laptop in 1 of 40 runs: in serialized mode the branch waiting on the meter gate can receive the gate after the shutdown ended the held branch's call, open a window and fail at once on the cancelled token, so a third step is recorded `incomplete`; `AssertIncomplete`, `Shutdown_marks_in_flight_steps_incomplete` and the Specs Ctrl+C step now assert the invariant through `RunOrchestrationFixtures.AssertShutdownDuringFirstFanOut` (2 or 3 steps of the same task and repeat 1, the Planner first and `ok`, every other step a distinct Researcher or Writer with outcome `incomplete`, no Reviewer and no later task or repeat, the console listing the same steps in file order), with `run.status` `incomplete`, exit 5, the single error line and the time bound unchanged. ## User decisions after the M3 exit

- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (1) cut order: Gate M3 shows S 26.2 h and the literal rule 4 applies Level 1 C1 to C8; apply, or hold again and re-measure at the M4 exit (the window velocity has held at about 32 to 33 MUST h per day for three gates); recommended: hold, with AJ-093 and AJ-088 re-admitted only if M4 shows slack.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (2) the NVIDIA model id: `nvidia/nemotron-nano-3-30b-a3b` is not enabled for the account (404) while `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning` answers; change `Tiers:nvidia:ModelId` and `Judge:ModelId` in config/appsettings.json (a design and prompt consistency check is needed, since the prompt names the model), or enable the function on the NVIDIA account; recommended: the user checks the account first, and the config change (one line each) is applied at the M4 kickoff. Stated for the record (peer review r-3): with a reasoning judge model and no reasoning-off prefix on the judge tier, the 32-token cap of `Judge:MaxOutputTokens` ends every judgment as `parse-error` instead of running unbounded, the intended failure mode.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (3) empty completions: whether a 200 response with no content gets a step flag (for example `empty-output`) or an outcome of its own, so the report table and the dashboard show it (today only the quality reason says it); recommended: a flag, scheduled in M4 with AJ-104's messages.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (4) the judge failure warning: add the HTTP status and the reason, as the step failure message has them; recommended: do it in M4 with AJ-104.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (5) the AJ-083 cost-format amendment: confirm or revert; recommended: confirm.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (6) the AJ-092 optional NITs (a zero-length step followed by another step at the same instant; the refusal tests' 60 s hang guard) and the M3 residuals listed in the carried items: defer to M7 unless the user wants them now; recommended: defer to M7.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (7) the remote branch `milestone/M3` is deleted after the merge per kickoff decision 3; no decision needed, recorded; recommended: none needed.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (8) the self-judging disclosure rule (peer review M-1): keep the shipped three-state line that prints the compared model ids (yes when every judged step's model id equals the judge id, not determinable from the model ids otherwise, not judged when nothing was judged), or add a declared same-model rule (a configuration statement that the judge runs the same model as a tier, labelled declared); recommended: keep the three-state line, which asserts only what the code can check.
- 2026-10-24 (M3 exit), (9) `costPerQualityPoint` is labelled model-judged although one input is an estimated cost (the AJ-074 amendment; peer review open question): keep one label, or label it estimated because a cost-derived value is an estimate, or carry both inputs' labels in the reason; recommended: estimated, decided at the M4 kickoff before any published report.
